original_question: Let G be a combinatorial graph, let alpha(G) denote the size of a maximum independent set of G, and let alpha_1(Gamma(G)) denote the largest size of a 1-independent set in its continuous counterpart Gamma(G), where points of the continuous edges may be chosen as set members and any two chosen points must be at distance at least 2. Is n/2 a tight universal upper bound on the ratio alpha_1(Gamma(G))/alpha(G), and how does this ratio behave on special graph classes?
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, in the unnumbered open-problem paragraph titled Relaxation gap for r = 1: after defining α1(Γ) and giving the nearby bound in Proposition 1, the paper asks whether n/2 is a tight upper bound for α1(Γ(G))/α(G), and immediately adds that structural properties of combinatorial graphs may affect this ratio on special cases/classes of graphs. This draft is targeting that specific open question, not a broader neighboring problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object and scope: it fixes the paper’s r = 1 setting, compares the classical independence number α(G) with the continuous 1-independence number α1(Γ(G)), correctly allows points from edge interiors to be chosen, uses the pairwise distance-at-least-2 condition, and includes both parts of the paper’s open question: the possible n/2 upper bound and the behavior of the ratio on special graph classes. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
missing_details: You should specify that G is a finite combinatorial graph with n = |V(G)| (the paper’s n/2 bound is a function of the number of vertices, so “universal upper bound” should be read as “for every n-vertex graph”). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

You should define Γ(G) exactly as in Definition 4: each edge uv of G is replaced by a unit-length continuous edge e_{u,v}, and the distance on Γ(G) is the shortest-path metric in the resulting topological space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

You should define α1(Γ(G)) exactly as in Definition 9: it is the maximum cardinality of a set I of points of Γ(G) such that d(p,q) ≥ 2 for all distinct p,q in I. The selected points are not restricted to the original vertex set. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

The quantifier should be explicit: the paper is asking whether α1(Γ(G))/α(G) ≤ n/2 for all such graphs G, motivated by the complete-graph example K_n with n even, where α(K_n) = 1 and α1(Γ(K_n)) ≥ n/2 via midpoints of a matching. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

The phrase about “special graph classes” should remain noncommittal: the paper does not single out specific families here, but only says that structural properties of combinatorial graphs are expected to influence the ratio and that it is interesting to study special cases/classes of graphs. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

If you want the question to be literally stand-alone, you should exclude the empty graph (or assume n ≥ 1) so that the ratio α1(Γ(G))/α(G) is defined; this is implicit in the paper’s discussion of n-vertex graphs. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
refined_question: Let G be a finite combinatorial graph with n = |V(G)| ≥ 1, and let Γ(G) be the continuous graph obtained by replacing each edge uv of G by a unit-length continuous edge e_{u,v} and equipping the resulting point set with the shortest-path metric. Let α(G) denote the maximum size of an independent vertex set of G, and let α1(Γ(G)) denote the maximum cardinality of a set I of points of Γ(G) such that d(p,q) ≥ 2 for all distinct p,q ∈ I. Is it true that α1(Γ(G))/α(G) ≤ n/2 for every G, and if so is this bound tight? More specifically, how do structural properties of G affect this ratio on special classes of graphs? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
justification: The draft clearly targets the paper’s Section 3.1 open problem on the r = 1 relaxation gap, rather than the other open problems in the paper. The nearby context needed to make the question paper-faithful is Definition 4 for Γ(G), Definition 9 for 1-independence and α1, Proposition 1 for the basic neighboring bound α1(Γ) ≤ |V|, and the complete-graph example that motivates the possible n/2 extremal ratio. The rewrite therefore stays narrowly within that exact open question and does not broaden to arbitrary r, approximability, or other continuous-graph parameters. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
